critical_evidence.evidence: The seller discloses non-competitive HPDE/TNIA sessions (Summit Point, and a track-cross at Dominion years ago) plus autocross 2-3 times a year. The seller states oil is checked before events and the car has never burned oil. There is no compression or leakdown data, and no oil-consumption test.
The seller reports the brake pads as the only modification. Exhaust tips look stock in the rear photos. There is no ECU/OBD readout confirming a stock calibration, and headers are not examined here.
NHTSA 18V772000 covers 2013 cars. This is a 2016 (VIN-decoded).

NHTSA 21V587000 is scoped to 2018-2019 in the profile; this is a 2016. Separately, the seller says the fuel pump was replaced under warranty in 2018 for the 'cricket' noise bulletin. That claim has no receipt shown.

documentation.rationale: Identity and terms are present: VIN given and matching the decode, clean-title and Carfax references, one-owner claim, and the odometer photo matches the listed mileage. On maintenance, a dated May 2024 service at 55,214 mi is shown in gallery documents. Missing: the full record set before 2024, receipts for the June 2026 brakes and the 2018 fuel pump, and coolant history. Underbody corrosion severity is not pinned down.

condition.rationale: Several items are disclosed: cosmetic chips and dings, upholstery wear and stains (visible on the rear seat), and some underbody corrosion that a bidder called 'crunchy' on suspension parts. Track and autocross use is admitted on the original clutch. On the other side, the photos show straight panels, stock ride height, a clean interior overall and no check-engine light. The dated 2024 fluid service and fresh rotors help. Nothing is inspection-verified.

price_value.rationale: The $13,500 bid sits below the $16,400 comp (a 2017 Limited at 46.9k mi), but the reserve is unmet or unknown and final-hour bidding will likely rise. Higher mileage, disclosed track use, corrosion and the original clutch justify a discount against that comp. At a hammer near $15-16k this is roughly fair value, not a bargain.

mission_fit.rationale: It meets the bridge brief: a manual, naturally aspirated, Toyota co-developed car well inside the $10-19k ideal band, and easy to resell. It is a secondary candidate behind the Z3 3.0i. The disclosed track use slightly weakens the 'reliable, easy life' case.

logistics.rationale: The car is in Warrenton, VA, across the country from Carmel, and the auction closes within the hour. No PPI can happen before a binding bid. The Cars & Coffee viewing is local only. CA registration and smog should be feasible for a stock-appearing car.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: WR Blue, 6-speed manual, Limited trim with LSD and heated Alcantara seats, essentially stock, and one owner. It is desirable but not rare. The track-pad fitment and disclosed track use slightly dilute its originality.

evidence.mission_note: A manual, naturally aspirated BRZ in the ideal price band fits the enthusiast bridge brief as a secondary candidate. The disclosed track use and corrosion, combined with an imminent remote close, make inspection discipline the issue rather than fit.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: the VIN matches the decode, the odometer photo reads 58,717 against the stated 58,800, and a clean VA title, clean Carfax and single owner since June 2016 are referenced. One dated service at 55,214 mi (May 2024) is documented. Observed issues are disclosed rather than hidden: HPDE track sessions and regular autocross on the original clutch and engine, some underbody corrosion that bidders noticed on suspension parts, track-oriented brake pads, upholstery wear and stains visible in the photos, and cosmetic chips. The BRAKE lamp in the cluster photo is most likely the parking brake but is unconfirmed. Engine health after track use (compression, leakdown, consumption) and corrosion severity remain open and are the two items that matter most. Both recall items on the model list fall outside this 2016's model years. The auction is a reserve sale ending within the hour in Virginia, so no inspection can precede a binding bid. The high bid of $13,500 is below the $16,400 comp for a lower-mileage 2017 Limited, but the final price is not yet set.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller now for close-up underbody photos, tire date codes and the pre-2024 records. If they cannot arrive before the 12:06 PM PDT close, do not bid, and watch for a relist or no-sale that would allow a Virginia PPI with a compression/leakdown test.
